en: Nārāyaṇa created the four-faced [Brahmā]
And the four-faced [Brahmā] took over and created Śankara
Taking precedence, I have announced the deep meaning
putting forth an antāti:
You examine [it well] and receive [it] without spilling
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative
perfective aspect, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
perfective aspect, third person, masculine singular

en: While examining, they say there is but one god
Nobody knows His greatness
This much is the conclusion of the examined meaning
Grace appears from Him with the discus
for those who performed any [kind of] penance
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, dative, third person, honorific
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular, locative

en: Who will know [His] reclining on the milk, [His] dwelling in Raṅgam of old
[His] sleeping on the banyan[-leaf], the world’s unique Essential Principle
the celestials’ true Essence, the rare Meaning [lying on the] water
the way I have known [Him]?
Is it acceptable to say that [Śiva] who concealed the river in [his] matted locks
Shares [supremacy] with the King of the celestials?
I have summed Him up, who is the word for all meanings, our Lord
Him who has stood without another [to match Him]
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine singular
participial noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative

en: O Māl with shoulders [and] curved nails that tore open
the chest of the unvanquished [Hiraṇyakaśipu], who added boons [for himself]!
Know that You Yourself are the four rare [kinds of life]
by lifting [the worlds] up one day [after] drawing [them] in
[at the end of] the yugas!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
negative, participial noun, third person, masculine singular
participial noun, third person, masculine singular

en: The Jains do not know [the truth], the Buddhists have forgotten [it]
Śiva’s priests [are] insignificant people
To tell [the truth], those [who] do not praise the fragrant Dark [Lord]
Mālavaṉ, Mādhavaṉ
are therefore base people now
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative

en: Whether it comes today, or tomorrow
or be slightly delayed now, Your grace is mine
Look, O Nārāyaṇa! Indeed, I do not exist without You
[and] You do not exist without me [either]
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

en: O my heart! [In times of] need, there is no companion other than
the red-eyed Māl with a bow that defeated Śiva
Him with sharp arrows that destroyed the might of the Laṅkā
of [Rāvaṇa] with a cluster of ten heads, who did not reach [Rāma]
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular

en: Having had [his] wants fulfilled, the four-faced [Brahmā] poured water
from the pitcher on that day
[and] praising [Him] with Vedic mantras
[he] washed the red feet of the Lord of the Universe so that [the water] entered
the head of [Śiva] with a stained throat
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
perfective aspect, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular

en: Are we not capable of seeing the golden body of Him on the bed
that is the beautiful [but] hostile erpent which spits fire
hearing the loud noise then?
[Brahmā] on the big flower [and Śiva] with long matted locks
are not capable of praising [Him]
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular

en: Let the mouths praise! Let the eyes see! Let the ears hear!
Do bow down lowering the crown [of your heads]
joining unfailingly [your] bounteous hands in reverence
and meditating upon my ancient Māl with a long crown
with abundant tulsi wound around with cool flowers
You decided that the people—who, having become experts in [scriptures]
do not regard [You]—should go and fall into the four [types of wombs]
O You who liberated the moon [from its] evil!
You decided to send the discus to free the [elephant] from the hold of the big
pond-dwelling crocodile
You decided upon a twin liberation with the[ir] two [older states] leaving [them]
gloss: negative, participial noun, third person, honorific
participial noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: Not knowing the method that grants liberation, O you who wander around
afflicting [your] bodies, making skeletons [of them]
[by] standing [in penance] [and] eating [thereafter]!
Nārāyaṇa is the true Essence who grants liberation, the First Cause [as per] the Vedas
the good object [of enjoyment] for the celestials
Listening to the words of the cadaver[-like] people [of other] religions
—who did not get to utter the names of Tirumāl, [called] Nārāyaṇa
He who rules me, He who protects [one] from reaching hell—
many [people] will sink, feeling the desire [to follow them]
If [you] are able to offer numerous blossoms, bow down at, and praise
the feet of Him who stepped over the earth so that many gods praised
the very means [through which] Mārkaṇḍeya discovered the condition experienced
by the [venomed] liquid-throated [Śiva] will come [to you too], see!
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular

en: My heart will remain stable because of Him who hid the earth with the chariot wheel
so that it was hidden, as the sun vanished
so that many kings died in battle
as the highest King of the gods Himself became [their] enemies on that day
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine singular, instrumental

en: In a former yuga, under the shade of a banyan tree
[Śiva] with true penance told the four people about
the path of dharma that is his means of worshipping
Him who measured the worlds, Him who reclined on the sea
Him who slept on the banyan [leaf]
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, honorific, dative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
participial noun, third person, honorific, masculine, accusative
participial noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative
participial noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative

en: The penance of the people who join
those who keep praising in a distinct way
the Lion who sliced the chest of the inimical Rākṣasa into two
with [His] sharp claws
Shall overcome them
gloss: participial noun, third person, honorific, accusative

en: Are [You] not [the Lord] with a discus who rendered useless
The boons [that the Rākśasas] obtained from Brahmā by performing penance?
You are the one who gladly protects us; You are [our] protection
You are the one who grants Vaikuṇṭha to all the souls!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular, instrumental
participial noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative

en: You are all the worlds; [all] that remains is [due to] Your grace
You are the God of gods [with] penance; You are all these:
the burning fire, the big mountains, the eight directions
the two lights of the sky
gloss: participial noun, third person, neuter plural

en: Is this the cave mouth that opened and spat fire out?
Are these the fiery-circle[-like] eyes?
Is this the beauty that the Lord of the unblinking [gods]—
who appeared flaring up [like] fire—presented flaring up [as] a lion?
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, neuter plural

en: The Essence of the seven worlds [and their] attributes
the [First] Cause, who, as a child, as a fish, protects the souls
is the Beautiful One; He is the One with a lion form
Humble [yourselves] at the feet of the Intimate [Lord]!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular

en: Is there a need [for us] to sow seeds in the ancient fields of
the bhakti Ploughman who subdued the bulls?
The passing water[-bearing] clouds is reminiscent of the sacred body of the dark Māl
who is like black clouds that rise in clusters
You shone in all four hues, white, [red] gold, green, [and] black
You despised [Madhu and Kaiṭabha] so that both perished
Becoming the commander of the [Pāṇḍava] army, [You] praised the angry, belligerent
Man with white horses [Arjuna]
[in such a] way that [he] ended the war [as per Your] heart’s [wish]
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative

en: You acquired the earth by means [of begging], not considering [it a big task]
Besides, [You] brought to an end the inimical ways
of the self-conceited Mahābalin who eats diamonds
melting [them] by [medicinal] means, oh!
Is there anything that will come out of such [acts for You]?
See! [Śiva] with tied-up matted locks is witness
to the fact that I do not have any other [deities] to worship
O sea-hued [Lord]! Look, see to it that
I am able to learn about [You] forever!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, honorific, accusative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

en: O simpletons! Will I—who am able to see [His] garlanded, large red feet
which the ash-besmeared [Śiva] himself could not see—
esteem as a blessing [anything]
other than this, [namely,] my simple heart, which Māl Himself entered?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, neuter singular
pronominalised noun, first person, singular, dative

en: This, the bridge that was built so that the might of Laṅkā would be ruined
This, the felling of the animal Vālin
These are the joys of [Rāma] who dispatched [arrows]
In such a way that [His] bow became bent
So that Laṅkā became subservient
So that the body of Rāvaṇa with cool garlands slid [down]
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine singular

en: If one considers [it], [Rāma]—who, getting very angry, discharged one arrow
so that [Kumbhakarṇa], with a yojanā’s [distance] between [his] one eyebrow
and the [other] fell—
is the one with a pleasing, lustrous, and great form
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
participial noun, third person, masculine singular

en: [The Lord] of Raṅgam is the one who rules me
He guards me against reaching the stage [of the world]
He stood [and] sat in my heart
Will [He then] recline on the serpent-bed upon the sea?
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine singular

en: Formerly, it was Nārāyaṇa who destroyed the curse
placed by the four-faced [Brahmā] on Hara-Śiva on this earth
O demons who do not extol the Lord of celestials!
If one speaks of the wonder of the foetus that is born
[it would be] a [long] story
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, masculine singular

en: Stories [and] meanings are in the sacred mind of Kṛṣṇa
Not getting caught in [His] surpassing qualities
—without spending time [otherwise] [even] for a moment—
is indeed a matter of distress!
Reach the feet of Him with excellent qualities
gloss: finite verb, third person, neuter plural

en: Kicking the cart with a foot, conquering the snake
catching the elephant and braking [its tusks], drinking poison from
the demoness’s breasts
smashing the mighty bulls’ necks for the sake of Piṉṉai with beautiful red coral lips
[and] shoulders
He later became king [as per His] intention
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, feminine singular, dative
perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: My intention is to extol [the Lord] who resides in Kōṭṭiyūr
My intention is that good [should] happen [to me]
[So] would I loathe [the Lord] who lives in Veṅkaṭam?
[Would I loathe] the feet of Him whose nature is to destroy
the body[-induced] karman [and] suffering
so that [they] do not approach [me]?
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative
participial noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular

en: [The Lord] from the great Allikkēṇi—by the great Mayilai
where high waves come and dash [against the shores]
graciously lies silently on the bed of serpent with five heads [and] mouths—
will not open [His] mouth
Is [this due to] the weariness of measuring the world with [His] feet?
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular

en: On the snake bed in Kuṭantai, Veḵkā, [and] the sacred Evvuḷ
On the snake bed in Raṅgam, Pēr, [and] Aṉpil
on the snake bed on the milky ocean
lies the primordial tall Māl
[in order] to be in the minds of those who embrace [Him]
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine singular

en: The sky, the moving fire, the wind, the big seas, the big mountains
The moving [sun] with hot rays, the cool moon
the clouds that stay above, people, the eight quarters, [all] pervading [things]
The [cosmic] egg: [these] are the effects of Tirumāl’s will
He whose hue is that of the water of the dashing sea
Entraps humans devoid of uplifting [in] the six religions
If [He] stirs up, any god’s arrogant deeds, any type of deeds
[and] summons [to gods in the sacrifices] will cease then [and there]
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, masculine singular

en: I will call the Lord of sacred Vēṅkaṭam in order to see [Him]!
I will draw the sacred kūṭal-circle so as to rejoin the mountain
where the elephants are startled and the snakes hide themselves
As the big waterfalls come descending, gathering gems during the rainy season
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative

en: I sang of Vēṅkaṭam thinking it is [the name of] a mountain
I [thus] stand having arranged for liberation. I stand thinking [about this]
I remain caught in the nets that are the feet of the Husband of the Lady of the Vedas
Who [Himself] remains caught in the nets that are the Vedas that are learned, see!
O You from Vēṅkaṭam to which [devotees] come in a cherishing way
As pearls drop off from the resounding waterfalls
and produce echo during the ōṇam festival! You have entered my heart
I desire to go and see that sacred Vēṅkaṭam
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular, vocative

en: Will you not go [and] worship the very lofty Vēṅkaṭam?
Due to [its] nature that constantly destroys karman
The four-faced [Brahmā] on the fragrant lotus and the three-eyed [Śiva]
forever praise [Him] there, placing lotuses [at His] feet
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular

en: In order to perform the [evening] service for Him
of Vēṅkaṭam in the North, whose peaks touch the clouds
[Śiva] who put the moon up [his] matted locks and [Brahmā] upon the lotus
Entered [the temple] at night
Having gathered everything [including] the umbrella
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular, accusative
participial noun, singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, masculine, singular, third person

en: O you young men! Go desiringly to the Vēṅkaṭam hills with groves
where stands the Young Man, who, in former times
became an infant placed on [Brahmā’s] laps, and
and went on counting the punishable Rākṣasa’ heads with [Its] feet
Vēṅkaṭam with cool waterfalls—
of [the Lord] who stands tall, being perceived everywhere
as one desiringly places flowers at the lotus feet
and affectionately stays as felled trees do
—is the treasure for the celestials and the terrestrials
gloss: lie down on the ground motionless as a tree
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, honorific, dative
pronominalised noun, third person, honorific, dative

en: If the world dances [going] around Veṅkaṭam—
where the hill-people take up bows
As the hunters surround from all sides
the elephant that at all times stretches out [its] trunk
saying ‘I shall place the big full moon as a beautiful lamp for Māl,’
—[it will be] good
Veṅkaṭam
Which contains yāḷis, murderous lions, gold, gems, pearls, flowering trees
forests where many gems whirl around joining the waters
monkeys, and hunters
is the town of the good sapphire-hued [Lord]
Veṅkaṭam is [the mountain] that the celestials worship truth[fully]
Veṅkaṭam is [the mountain] that ends the disease of bodily troubles
Veṅkaṭam is the mountain of [the Lord] who protects the celestials
using His discus-weapon so that the Rakshasas fall
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, honorific, accusative
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: [May] the uttering of the sacred names---
of the Lord who churned [the ocean] so that [the nectar] burst [through]
placing the mountain on the Tortoise and
tying Vāsuki around [it]
The Tortoise itself holding on to [its] top, with one hand
so that [the water] does not shake---
Be the speech for everyone
I have learnt the means of not [having] death, or the cruel karman
or evil diversity approach
The words of Kṛṣṇa who reclines on the riverbank
The Dark One who reclines on the ocean
rest in my heart
O You of the hue of ironwood-flowers from the uplands!
Who ever is equal to me? Our Lord is His own equal, but not [mine]!
The others do not know You
Is the whole sky [of equal] value to my mind?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Worthy people will become devoted servants for a price
accept [and] receive [others’] diseases, [and] turn themselves
into human sacrificial gifts so that [someone else protects their] head!
Those who do not extol the King who drank poison from [Pūtanā’s] breasts
as being distinguished
Are ignorant people who experience sins
gloss: negative, participial noun, third person, honorific
negative, participial noun, third person, honorific

en: I do not have a god other than Kākutstha
who ruined the might of Laṅkā of the ignorant people
Do not accept evil gods, those that are not gods
[and] gods that have no holiness/Śrī as [being] divine
gloss: negative, participial noun, third person, honorific
participial noun, third person, honorific, accusative

en: All the learning of people who do not know that
the tall Māl is everyone - [namely,] that Deity who stands among the gods
the ancient creator who stands [among] the trinity among those gods
and He who stands as everyone—
is inferior
gloss: verbal noun, present tense, third person, neuter singular
negative, participial noun, third person, honorific
verbal noun, third person, neuter singular

en: People who stand at the entrance of [other] immortals [gods]
always worshipping [their] feet, will have intermediate joy
O tall Māl with a body like the ocean-water that surrounds [the earth]!
Who is able to recite [the glories of] Your feet?
Not [just] that man or this man: look, no one equals the Father of the bodiless Kāma!
[Śiva] who drank poison from the ocean of brackish water
Stood by Bāṇa saying [that it was his] duty
and lost together [with him]
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: If one speaks [the truth], [Kṛṣṇa], who bent the big lime tree
Is [both] the good karman and the bad karman that remain with [us]
The celestials, the Rakshasas, and the earth that are nearby
are Him who prospers in my heart. What is there that is not [Him]?
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, neuter singular

en: I have produced love for Him who lives in my heart
our Lord the Dispeller of darkness, Him who, one day in the past, measured the earth
so that the kings were afraid
Him who lives in my heart, Him who flourished by ending the cruel karman
of [Śiva] on the bull who does not have [Him in his heart]
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: O You who are love! O You who are the rare nectar!
O You who are joy to me, a servant! O You who are everything!
O Husband of the golden Lady! O my Keśava with resplendent lustre!
I, a servant, am a servant to You who rule [over me] without evil
gloss: pronominalised noun, first person, singular, dative
participial noun, second person, singular, dative

en: O You who wander about looking for servants!
Always see the nature of me who wander about looking for [Your] feet
O You from Raṅgam who become a hard[-to-find] meaning to those who listen!
I will not leave off desiring You [in my] heart
gloss: participial noun, second person, singular, vocative
participial noun, third person, honorific, dative
pronominalised noun, third person, singular, vocative

en: Afflictions of the mind will not approach
If one accepts Madhusūdana as the refuge for oneself
Today, He who ruled the seven worlds remaining together
came [to me]. The wealth remains as one [with me] is only for me!
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: Those who—[not] having adorned themselves with and borne
the garland of cool tulasi swarmed by bees, of Śrīdhara, on whose chest Śrī stays—
do not know that the side where Śrī stays is the Cause [of the world]
Will proclaim those [gods that] stayed in wombs [as being the Cause] to the ignorant
gloss: participial noun, third person, negative, honorific
participial noun, third person, honorific, negative, dative

en: I have spent time speaking of, writing about
Reading, hearing about, bowing to, worshipping, and showing devotion to
You on the cruel serpent that spoke extensively about the movement
of stellar constellations
Therefore, I have borne patiently [with this life]
Placing what is [called] flowers and bowing, won’t you extol
Him with gold makara-shaped ear-rings, the primordial Lord
The Master, the Good [Lord], Nārāyaṇa, Him with words that sever our seven births?
Reciting [them] is [our] means
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative

en: I have resolved in my heart that [this] is the means:
tell [me], is there no place in Vaikuṇṭha for me
who am thinking, as much as [I] can, of the garland of names
of the handsome Māl, Mādhava?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative
participial noun, first person, singular, dative

en: [From] today onwards, my heart is the abode of
the tall Māl who once [lay in] the bed that is the hooded serpent
I, who am sharp, shall not consider the moon-bearer [Śiva] along with Aja-Brahmā
as true [gods]; I shall not serve [them] [thanks to God’s] might
gloss: negative, imperfective aspect, first person, singular

en: May [my] nature to well extol, [all] day long, Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of speech
The Lord of knowledge, the great One
[give] strength or not
[give] high birth or a faulty [one]
‘Look, do not swerve [from this]: leave like good people
bowing down to the human beings who
do not worship a foreign [god] even if they forget God,’ said Yama
In the ears of [his] messengers, summoning [them]
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Look, the name of the red-eyed Māl is what is bliss to the ears
And it is the place [of refuge] for the [people of the] earth
I have met [the Lord] who is the complete meaning of poetry
If [we] look into [it], that much is the essence of the Vedas
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative

en: I am not the only one to know today that
[the Lord] who became a unique Boar, dug the earth out, lifted [it] up
and bore [it] on [His] tusks
is the Child, [who], turning into a matchless person, went there [to Balin]
and subdued the wide world
gloss: present tense, first person, singular, participial noun

en: Those words uttered on that day by the Dark [Lord]
who is distant, nearby, small, very big, the Cowherd
the King of Dvārakā—
Those who do not know [them] in [this] world
are [God’s] enemies devoid of true knowledge
gloss: pronominalised noun, masculine, singular, third person
pronominalised noun, masculine, singular, third person
pronominalised noun, masculine, singular, third person
pronominalised noun, masculine, singular, third person
negative, participial noun, third person, honorific

en: The words that state that the householder dharma, or else, the ascetic dharma
is the place [of refuge]
and those that [claim] non-dharmic [means are the refuge] are not words
[of authoritative evidence]
Nārāyaṇa is [all] the good dharmas and the great penance of the four Vedas
Who says it is not [so]?
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, third person
participial noun, third person, neuter plural

en: Who would know the greatness of [the Lord] with the great discus
who swallowed and spat out all the worlds?
[Śiva] with the throat dense with blackness [and] the eight-eyed [Brahmā]
Will not perceive the location of the ancient heaven that He had placed
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: My tongue shall not extol anything but the large-bodied, wondrous [Lord]
Who, valuing the shiny snake [Sumukha]—
which, not being equal to [its] chiefly enemy [Garuḍa]
reached the sea of water with leaping waves, considering [it a refuge]—
hoisted [it] upon [Garuḍa’s own] powerful body!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative

en: ‘I shall not sing of mankind with [my] tongue
[My] songs [will] be on the red feet of the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha
who did not [condescend] to be pleased, as [Śiva] with fire-like red matted locks
went carrying flowers to always extol [Him] as much as [he] could
so that good occurred [to him].’
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: Poetry and ordered [texts], excellent stories, and the many meanings
The acquired fire, the wide sky
The Manu [smṛti], and the four aural Vedas that are heard
are [elements] whose real nature came into existence
through the māyā of the wondrous [Lord]
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: Even if He—the ocean-natured [Lord] who filled up the vast sea with rocks—
Does not know my real nature
He saw and set [His] unchanging heart [on me]
So that the cruel karman that had seized me leaves
Oh, any karman shall perish [by His] seeing!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect

en: As Umā instructed the ascetic [Śiva] who struck Kāma’s body
[he] kept listening to the names of [the Lord] with a long crown
[adorned with] a flower garland swarmed by bees and was fully moved there
[If we] examine [this]: what will happen to those who have seen and worshipped
[Him directly]?
gloss: participial noun, third person, honorific, dative
pronominalised noun, third person, honorific, dative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: Those who, thinking out of love of the Primordial Lord
are able to place [Him] in [their] excellent hearts
Will desire their bodies fitted [with souls] to give [them] distress
wishing to see their Vaikuṇṭha swiftly
Swiftly reach Kṛṣṇa, who guarded against [sorrows], protected
and sheltered the world, concealing [it in His belly]
as floods spread [everywhere] on a day in the past
The entrance doors of cruel hell were destroyed
hearing the singing [and] the dancing of the [people of the] world
spreading [everywhere]
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, neuter plural

en: Sowing the good Tamil as a seed, becoming the language [that I] learned
becoming absorbed [in me], You caused my heart to sprout
I have become freed from the mind whose work is to bewilder
which [sometimes] thinks, ‘The heart is a door [preventing the vision of Him]’
And [at other times] thinks, ‘it is possible to see [Him]’
The father of Kāma, the King—whom Śiva, the four-faced [Brahmā]
and the like, who [seek to] extol [Him] placing blossoming flowers
cannot extol [Him by] expressing [themselves]—
became absorbed in my heart. Is there a goodness equal to this?
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: [The Lord] with the discus, the Black-hued [Lord] becomes [all] the kings
the celestials, heaven, mercy [itself], the people, the mother, everything else
to those who depend upon [Him]. [And yet] not [feeling] satisfied
He Himself gives [all and] then, [He] does acts of wonder
gloss: participial noun, third person, honorific, dative
participial noun, third person, singular, masculine, negative

en: I who bear love—[so that my] occupation is to always worship
the King with feet [adorned with] resounding anklets, Kṛṣṇa—
do not have a scattered mind
I rival Śiva [in terms of knowledge but] he is no match for me
My occupation is to extol the names of the ancient Māl
My time shall be spent [doing] that
The Expert Archer who destroyed the arrogance
of Vālin, the king of monkeys, the mighty one with excessive anger
is in [my] heart
O good heart! See, the Highest [Lord] is [there to protect]
He is [there to protect] at all times, see! See, He is in the minds of those
who think of [Him]!
See, the Lord who is His [own] equal is [there to protect]
He is the Supreme Lord for me, a destitute person, and for the likes of me!
Be enlightened!
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, first person, singular, dative

en: Who is [the Lord] who protects [the cowherds], having eaten
the conventionally established feast
served for Indra, [heaped up] like the big Himalayan mountains?
[It is] He who has seen the [different] creeds, He who protects them
He who swallowed the worlds along with living beings
as well as the black-throated [Śiva and] the four-faced [Brahmā]?
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
singular, masculine, perfective aspect, participial noun

en: It is only those who sing the names of [the Lord]—who ends pain
Running after [the souls] when [they] run away taking the[ir] life-breath
[with them], leaving behind [their] bodies—
And who contemplate so that actions cease
who [reach] felicity
As for the lives of those with bondages [linked to] petty creeds
They are unprofitable
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, plural, imperfective aspect

en: I have learned of one [means] that is unfailing:
Those who live seeing and bowing down to the people
who unerringly meditate upon and worship [all] day
the feet of [the Lord] on the milky ocean
shall overcome the karman intertwined [with their souls]
open Heaven and sit high with distinction [there]
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, honorific, accusative

en: People who wish to rule over heaven sitting [there] in distinction
are those who properly place many flowers by the side of [the Lord of] Vēṅkaṭam
[But] will live perfectly [compared to] the above those who belong to the people
who become devoted [to Him], watching the thoughts that occur [to Him]
and prostrate themselves in worship before Him
Those who are His people
—who, saying ‘We shall reach the black-hued [Lord]’s lotus feet’
placing flowers at [His] lotus feet and bowing down [to them] —
are the immortal [gods] to everyone, to [Brahmā] on the lotus
to the immortals, to [Śiva] who wears dancing snakes
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, dative
participial noun, third person, honorific, dative

en: [Being] protected since the day [I] was in the womb
I never forget [Him, whether] standing [or] sitting
placing the tall Māl in my heart
and becoming the slave of Śrīdhara, Him on whose chest Śrī sat forever
O King who shows favour by giving bodies to the many souls
as [their] bodies perish there [during the deluge]!
I shall never forget [Your] protection. I shall remain thinking [everything] is Kaṇṇaṉ
O You who are superior [due to Your] qualities! Those who have understood the truth
will not dare give You up!
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, honorific, perfective aspect

en: O You whose bed is the snake with bright hoods
—who, understanding that the dissident [foes] [should] turn into ashes—
felled [them] in the battlefield, giving a little [help to the Pāṇḍavas]!
Please be gracious to me, a servant!
If [one] accepts [it], even neem becomes a dish. What will those
who have understood the truth not do?
gloss: participial noun, third person, honorific, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, first person, singular, dative

en: I have accepted service [to Him]; I have fallen [away from] the affliction of birth
I have been filled [with devotion so that] the [other] immortal [gods]
do not to get close [to me]
Giving up the borrowed land and the earthly land
I have become filled [with desire] to now see the land of the place located
above [these]
I have now understood [You as being] Śiva’s and the four-faced [Brahmā]’s God!
I have now understood You, O our Lord! I have now understood
that You are the Cause, You are what was learnt, You are what is learnt
You are Nārāyaṇa of good actions. I have well understood [all this]
